# Cantonese Wordnet candidate source attribution

This project-generated file accompanies unmodified upstream `cantown.xml` and
`README.md` from [Cantonese Wordnet](https://github.com/lmorgadodacosta/CantoneseWN),
commit `6434cbc1d692d3061266352aa223a8df4a9c883e`.

Created and maintained by Joanna Ut-Seong Sio and Luis Morgado da Costa. The
upstream README and XML `Lexicon` element explicitly declare Creative Commons
Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0). Original source authors retain their
rights. Retaining this source does not imply their endorsement of this IME or
independent approval of every reading.

Canonical citation requested by the source:

Sio, Joanna Ut-Seong & Morgado da Costa, Luis. (2019). Building the Cantonese
Wordnet. In *Proceedings of the Tenth Global Wordnet Conference (GWC 2019)*,
pp. 206–215. Wroclaw, Poland. https://aclanthology.org/2019.gwc-1.26/

The complete standard license text is retained in `LICENSE-CC-BY-4.0.txt`.
The canonical terms are https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/ .
The direct legalcode text endpoint returned HTTP 403 during preparation, so the
exact complete CC BY 4.0 legal text was copied from the project's already
retained, hash-verified TypeDuck source `LICENSE`, which contains that standard
license without TypeDuck-specific additions. This copies license text only;
it does not introduce TypeDuck dictionary data into this source snapshot.
The source lock records the exact retained-file provenance and checksum.

No upstream XML or README bytes were changed. This attribution file and
`parser-attested-bases.json` are project-generated metadata, separate from the
raw originals. The parser inventory is frozen against database SHA-256
`3fccc5bcf45cbb676b8a1a51e2030d418803af64b3cd5c0ae7d67cf90a4711bb`.

Status: **candidate source preparation only**. The source is not imported or
enabled by default. These files represent no linguistic/mapping approval,
frequency measurement, completeness claim or native package update.

Proposed future scope is only `Lexicon` id `cantown-yue` with language `yue`:
explicit word/Jyutping `Form` fields paired with the `Lemma` in the same
`LexicalEntry`. The original XML also includes `cantown-en`, an English lexicon
with five explanatory entries and five empty forms. That lexicon is excluded,
not counted as Cantonese data. Definitions, semantic relations, examples,
companion corpus and media are not selected as lookup data. Do not infer missing
readings, borrow readings across lemmas, silently repair spelling/tone notation,
or assign pronunciation frequency from text-level counts. A future import must
state its transformations and account for empty, rejected and variant forms.
Any new character readings are direct-lookup candidates until separately reviewed
for phrase encoding. All fields remain present in the preserved raw XML.

CC BY 4.0 components may be included, with their source license and attribution
preserved, in the project's separately documented CC BY-SA 4.0 combined dictionary
adaptation. The original components retain their licenses; application code is
separate. A future selection must propagate the source notice into product
notices before redistribution.

Retrieved: 23 October 2026, Asia/Hong_Kong.
